capability.title: Diagnose and harden cross-layer integrations
capability.summary: I trace failures across application, service, and protocol boundaries, then make identity, completion, and failure behavior explicit.

blocks.body:
## Follow the operation across its boundaries

An integration can appear healthy at one end while failing at the next: an image is saved but never reaches the gallery, or a window is listed but supplies the wrong preview. I investigate the complete route from the initiating action to the visible result.

The fixes below span compositor identity, capture negotiation, and event delivery. Each gives a concrete boundary responsibility for the behavior that went wrong.

## Make the capture source unambiguous

Several windows can share an application ID and title. I connected each foreign-toplevel handle to its exact Wayfire view so those windows retain separate capture sources and previews.

A separate preview failure required explicit buffer-format negotiation between the compositor and image-copy client before copying a frame. The maintained capture implementation also reports unavailable views and copy failures through the protocol. Selecting the source, agreeing on the buffer, and completing the frame each have a defined outcome.

## Verify the result reaches its consumer

ComfyUI Conduit was saving generated outputs while ComfyUI Image Viewer stopped receiving live updates. I traced the break to an optional event adapter whose import still targeted the former package location.

After correcting the adapter, I verified the route from saved output through Redis to the gallery. The repair kept the host integration outside Conduit's package boundary, preserving the optional connection between the independently useful tools.

## Keep incomplete work distinguishable from success

I carry that same approach into service and AI integrations. Conduit's run records separate admission, execution, artifact capture, and delivery. AI Model Gateway retains discovery freshness and execution identifiers, while Narrative Scene Tracker records committed mutations and a terminal processing outcome.

Those records make a timeout, unavailable provider, rejected request, and uncertain upstream result distinguishable. They also give the next investigation a concrete place to start instead of requiring the entire failure to be reconstructed.
